title: He ordered death.
paragraphs:
He ordered death.
They chose to fear God instead.

And here’s the part that should shake you—
they did it quietly.

No applause.
No spotlight.
No guarantee they would survive the night.
Just a decision… in the hidden place.
Because the real battle in Exodus 1 was never just about babies.
It was about who you fear most.
And that question is still hunting hearts today.
Not all compromise looks evil at first.

“Just this once.”
“Just follow orders.”
“Don’t make it complicated.”
“Stay safe.”

And slowly…
your conviction starts to bend.

Your voice gets quieter.
Your obedience gets selective.
Your courage gets delayed.

Not loud rebellion.
But quiet surrender.

Not shouting “no” to God…
but softly ignoring Him.
In Exodus 1, a king sits on a throne, driven by fear and control.
“When you serve as midwife to the Hebrew women… if it is a son, you shall kill him.” (Exodus 1:16)
And into that darkness step two women most people would overlook:

No titles.
No armies.
No influence.
And here is the line that splits history in two:
“But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them…” (Exodus 1:17)

Not Pharaoh.
Not consequences.
Not death.
This is where many of us feel exposed.
We fear people more than we fear God.

We fear rejection.
We fear loss.
We fear discomfort.

So we stay silent when we should speak.
We comply when we should stand.
We shrink when we should shine.

They stood in a place soaked with pressure…
and chose obedience over safety.
Some scholars interpret their response to Pharaoh—when they said Hebrew women gave birth too quickly—as a strategic act of resistance, even deception. Others debate the ethics of it.
But Scripture does not praise their cleverness.
It praises their fear of God.
“So God dealt well with the midwives… and because the midwives feared God, he gave them families.” (Exodus 1:20–21)

In a culture where legacy mattered deeply…
God Himself becomes their rewarder.
The world may never have known their names.

Pharaoh built monuments.
God preserved midwives.
This story is not just about resisting evil systems out there.
It’s about confronting the Pharaoh within.
That voice inside you that says:

“Protect yourself at all costs.”
“Control everything.”
“Obey fear, not God.”
And no amount of willpower can overthrow it.
This is where the story explodes into the Gospel.
Because another ruler would rise generations later…
And once again, baby boys would be targeted.
“He sent and killed all the male children… two years old or under.” (Matthew 2:16)
Jesus grew up in a world just like ours—

Full of compromised leaders.
Silent crowds.
Hidden sins.

Where we drifted… He stood firm.
Where we feared… He obeyed.
Where we sinned… He remained pure.
He did something the midwives never could.

For every time we chose comfort over conviction.
For every silent compromise.
For every moment we feared people more than God.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” (1 Peter 2:24)
He walked out of the grave.
So now, the invitation is not:
Because the answer to that question will shape every decision you make.

Your obedience.
Your silence.
Your compromises.
Your courage.
Maybe today, you see it clearly.

Hiding truth.
Justifying sin.
Delaying obedience.

Turn from fear-driven living…
and surrender to Christ.
Because the same God who saw Shiphrah and Puah—
And He is not looking for perfection.
He is looking for surrendered hearts.
He is looking for people who fear Him more than anything else.
Even if the outcome is uncertain.
Because heaven writes down names the world forgets.
